clue.text: Correspondence, some enclosing a journal

indicators.note: enclosing says the word for 'some' wraps around the pieces that follow it

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you any?'
a log is a journal or daily record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: A collection of letters, some of which include a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosing' is the container signal. 'Correspondence' tempts as letters in the post, but here it means a likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogy is a likeness or parallel between two things, which is what correspondence means here.

clue.text: Tripe small number in Essex noshed regularly

parts.note: NO is the short form of number, the 'small' hinting at the abbreviation

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the words that follow, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the tripe a few people in Essex ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'in Essex noshed' to give NSENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is slang for rubbish or worthless talk, a close synonym of nonsense.

clue.text: Fellow is working for disreputable types

indicators.note: working means in operation, so the letters of the words before it are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A man is employed on behalf of shady characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges FELLOW IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowlifes are people regarded as morally or socially low, such as petty criminals.

clue.text: Signs of fear perhaps as some pubs go bust

indicators.note: go bust means fail and break apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Landlords feel dread as several pubs collapse into bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' rearranges SOME PUBS GO; 'perhaps' marks fear as only one cause of the bumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosebumps are small raised bumps on the skin brought on by cold, fright or excitement.

clue.text: PM over in Irish county

parts.note: Theresa May was the British Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister is finished in a western county of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland, in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Abuse left for one during current legal action

parts.note: current means fashionable or in vogue, which is IN

indicators.note: left for one means the letter for left takes the place of the letter for one

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Mistreatment of a leftist during an ongoing court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the I in SUIT for L, giving SULT; 'during' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone verbally is to insult them; both mean to speak offensively to a person.

clue.text: Understands it's stated patient individual requires cosmetic surgery

indicators.note: it's stated says a word is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: understands means knows, which sounds like nose
Job is the Old Testament figure famed for his patience under suffering

explanation.surface: A doctor realises a long-suffering patient needs a cosmetic operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is informal for rhinoplasty, surgery to reshape the nose for appearance.

clue.text: Excuse company essentially about mobile phone message

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its central letter

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a text is a message sent by mobile phone

explanation.surface: A firm sends a text message to explain itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes P, the middle letter of 'company'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one, much like an excuse.

clue.text: Airline service cross about supposedly unmissable target?

parts.note: BA is British Airways
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for cross is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Cabin crew grow cross about something they think impossible to miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROOD back to DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can't hit a barn door is a hopeless shot, since a barn's wide door is a huge mark.

clue.text: Skill of primarily kind old doctor in Cumbrian area

indicators.note: primarily says take the first letter of the word that follows
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: Cumbria is in North West England, abbreviated NW
Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of the BBC science fiction series

explanation.surface: The talent of a gentle elderly GP practising in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. Cumbria, home of the Lake District, is a county in the north-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Know-how is practical knowledge or expertise in doing something, a near synonym of skill.

clue.text: Greek character visits second gravestone, possibly

indicators.note: visits means goes into, so the Greek letter enters the word for second

parts.note: a moment is a second or very brief time
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person briefly calls by to look at a possible headstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visits' is the container signal; 'possibly' marks a gravestone as only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is a structure commemorating a person or event; a gravestone is one example.

clue.text: City Spice Girl barely missed

parts.note: Mel B is Melanie Brown, Scary Spice of the Spice Girls pop group

indicators.note: barely means stripped bare, so the word for missed loses its outer letters

parts.note: to have missed someone who died is to have mourned them

explanation.surface: A city where one of the Spice Girls was hardly missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' strips the ends from MOURNED, leaving OURNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Melbourne is a major city, capital of the Australian state of Victoria.

clue.text: Little old man retired, lacking in desire

indicators.note: lacking in says the word for desire is missing the letters that follow

parts.note: appetite is a desire or craving

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word for old man is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A small elderly man in retirement has lost his drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns PA into AP, which 'lacking in' takes out of APPETITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite describes someone or something small and dainty, especially a slight woman.

clue.text: Dicky wearing black tuxedo composed love letter

indicators.note: wearing means having something on, so the word for dicky has the other letters around it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of the word are arranged anew

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or weak, as in a dicky heart, so ILL

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky in a black dinner jacket wrote a romantic note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges the letters of 'tuxedo' into ETDOUX, and 'wearing' is the container signal. 'Dicky' looks like a name but is British slang for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is French for a sweet note, a love letter.

clue.text: Prime student to limit pressure before American exam

indicators.note: before places the pieces ahead of the letters for American
to limit means to hem in, so the word for prime and the student letter close around the pressure letter

parts.note: eleven is a prime number
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plates
P is the symbol for pressure in physics
US is the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A top pupil limits stress before a US test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to limit' puts P inside ELEVEN + L. The eleven-plus is the British exam taken at about eleven for entry to grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus is a selection test taken by children in their final primary school year in parts of the UK.

clue.text: Rum, maybe from Italy, son left half-finished

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees

indicators.note: half-finished says only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A drink of rum, perhaps from Italy, that a son left half-drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is not the drink but a small island in Scotland's Inner Hebrides; 'half-finished' leaves LE from 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Rum is an island in the Inner Hebrides, so it is an example of an isle.

clue.text: Entering southern strait, Norman occasionally is sleepy

indicators.note: entering says the picked letters go inside the name of the strait

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and southern England

indicators.note: occasionally says take only some letters at regular spacing, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A Norman occasionally drowsy as he sails into a channel on the south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks even letters from 'Norman' and 'Entering' is the container signal. The Solent separates the Isle of Wight from the Hampshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent is a formal word for drowsy, from the Latin for sleep.

clue.text: Ultimate plan I'm reticent somewhat to take up

indicators.note: take up says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A final scheme that I am rather reluctant to adopt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' finds LANIMRET in 'plan I'm reticent', and 'to take up' reads it upwards, as suits a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal means final or last, as at the end of a line, which is what ultimate means.

clue.text: Respectful First Lady has tear succeeding Republican

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the first lady and tear follow the party letter

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
a rent is a tear or rip in fabric

explanation.surface: A president's wife cries after a Republican wins the election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife, but it is Eve; 'tear' is a rip, not a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, especially in worship.

clue.text: Cook recipe accessed by upper-class gourmet

indicators.note: accessed by means entered by, so the class letter goes into the rearranged word
cook means to fiddle or falsify, so these letters are tampered with and rearranged

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage in British English

explanation.surface: A posh food lover follows a recipe in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges RECIPE into EPICRE, and 'accessed by' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is someone who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink, much like a gourmet.

clue.text: Play and series of books attracting magazine

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a series of books of the Bible
Hello! is a celebrity news magazine

explanation.surface: A stage show and a book series catch the eye of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'series of books' looks like a publisher's list, but it is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy about the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Got a load of fish, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals a word heard rather than seen, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: Someone hauled in a big catch of fish, or so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got a load of' is slang for looked at, not a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Get a load of is slang for take a good look at, so got a load of means watched or looked at.

clue.text: Traipses around externally impressive food shop

indicators.note: around means scattered about, so these letters are placed in a new order
externally says take only the outside letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone trudges about outside an impressive food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the letters of 'Traipses' into PATISSER, and 'externally' keeps only the outside letters of 'impressive'.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a bakery that sells pastries and cakes, a kind of food shop.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of extremely shady organisation

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporter sits below what it holds up, so the second piece comes after
extremely means at the extremes, so take the first and last letters

parts.note: to staunch a flow is to stem it

explanation.surface: A loyal backer of a very dodgy group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like loyal, but it is the verb meaning to stop a flow; 'extremely' gives SY from 'shady'.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised set of parts or methods, so a structure or organisation.

clue.text: Issue anaesthetic

definitions.meaning: a numbing agent makes something more numb

explanation.surface: Raising a question about a pain-killing drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading pronounces it NUM-er: something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a periodical is a number, and an anaesthetic numbs, making it a number.

clue.text: What fencers may use for protection?

definitions.text: What fencers may use for protection?

parts.words: What fencers may use for protection?
parts.note: fencers here are people putting up fences, who protect the wood with a preservative, not swordsmen

explanation.surface: What do swordsmen use to keep themselves safe?
explanation.walkthrough: Fencers suggests sword fighting with masks and jackets; here they are people who build fences and coat them in wood preservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tar oil painted on fence panels to protect the timber from rot.

clue.text: Approaching leader in race, draw level

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to, so the word for draw comes right before the leader letter

parts.note: a tie is a draw in a game

indicators.note: leader in says take the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Drawing near the front runner, a competitor pulls level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw level' reads as a single phrase; it splits, with 'level' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row, as in the tiers of a wedding cake or stadium.

clue.text: Caught golfer making embarrassing error

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Bernhard Langer is a German golfer, twice winner of the Masters

explanation.surface: A golfer is caught out making a humiliating mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A clanger is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a clanger is British slang for making a conspicuous, embarrassing blunder.

clue.text: Took over from daughter behind console

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the daughter letter follows the word for console

parts.note: to console someone is to relieve their distress
D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A parent replaced a games console that sat behind the daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'console' looks like a games machine, but it is the verb meaning to comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone on duty is to take over from them, as a sentry is relieved.

clue.text: Travelling a lot is origin of extended quarantine

indicators.note: travelling means on the move, so the letters move about into a new order
origin of says take the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Travelling widely is what started a long quarantine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' rearranges A LOT IS into ISOLAT, and 'origin of' gives E from 'extended'.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine someone is to keep them apart from others to stop disease spreading, that is to isolate them.
